root_cause.text: In btrfs_read_locked_inode(), the error path called iget_failed() while still holding a read-locked btrfs_path leaf, causing inode eviction to take delayed_node->mutex under a btree lock and creating an ABBA deadlock with delayed inode update paths that lock delayed_node->mutex before the subvolume btree.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message and added comment state that on inode lookup failure the function jumps to out “with a path that has a read locked leaf and then we call iget_failed()”; the patch fixes this by adding btrfs_release_path(path) before iget_failed(), and the lockdep trace shows iget_failed() -> btrfs_evict_inode() -> __btrfs_release_delayed_node() acquiring delayed_node->mutex while btrfs-tree-00 is already held.

intent_record.intent_summary: Release the btrfs path before `iget_failed()` in the inode read error path to prevent an ABBA deadlock during inode eviction.
intent_record.what: In the error path labeled `out:` of `btrfs_read_locked_inode()`, a new explanatory comment was added and a call to `btrfs_release_path(path);` was inserted immediately before the existing `iget_failed(vfs_inode);` call.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the function now releases any btree path/leaf lock held in `path` before invoking `iget_failed()`. This prevents inode eviction triggered by `iget_failed()` from running while still holding the path lock, avoiding an ABBA deadlock between delayed inode mutex locking and subvolume btree modification.

grouping_result.intent: Release the btrfs path before `iget_failed()` in the inode read error path to prevent an ABBA deadlock during inode eviction.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it releases the btrfs path/leaf lock before calling iget_failed() in the inode read error path, preventing the documented ABBA deadlock during inode eviction.

candidates.rationale: This error-path call triggers inode eviction while the function still holds the btrfs path leaf lock, leading eviction to take delayed_node->mutex under the btree lock and causing the ABBA deadlock described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This error-path call invokes inode eviction while the function still holds a read-locked btrfs_path leaf. Eviction can then acquire delayed_node->mutex under the btree lock, creating the ABBA deadlock with paths that take delayed_node->mutex before the subvolume btree.

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/inode.c b/fs/btrfs/inode.
bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet is sufficient because it includes the full error path of btrfs_read_locked_inode() and shows how it is called with a live struct btrfs_path from btrfs_iget_path()/btrfs_iget(). The vulnerable construct is present in the function's failure path: at label `out:` it does `iget_failed(vfs_inode);` and immediately returns, with no preceding `btrfs_release_path(path)`, `free_extent_buffer(path->nodes[0])`, path unlock, or equivalent cleanup. Earlier in the function, the code performs `ret = btrfs_lookup_inode(NULL, root, path, &location, 0);` and then accesses `leaf = path->nodes[0];`, so the function can hold a leaf in `path` when an error later occurs. Multiple later operations can fail after the lookup/path acquisition, for example `ret = btrfs_load_inode_props(vfs_inode, path);` and `ret = btrfs_add_inode_to_root(inode, true);`, both of which lead to `goto out;`. Therefore the function can call `iget_failed()` while still holding the btree path/leaf lock, matching the stated root cause. This commit only changes the parameter type from `struct inode *` to `struct btrfs_inode *` and replaces `BTRFS_I(inode)` uses with `inode`; it does not add any path release before `iget_failed()`, so the fix is not present.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because it includes the full error handling in btrfs_read_locked_inode(), which is the root of the vulnerability. The vulnerable construct is present: the new common error path ends with `out: iget_failed(inode); return ret;`, but there is no preceding cleanup that releases the btree path/leaf lock before calling `iget_failed(inode)`. Earlier in the function, the inode is looked up through a btree path (`ret = btrfs_lookup_inode(NULL, root, path, &location, 0);`, then `leaf = path->nodes[0];`) and the function continues parsing using that path. On several failures after this point, control goes to `goto out;`, including the newly added `ret = btrfs_add_inode_to_root(BTRFS_I(inode), true); if (ret) goto out;`. Since the snippet shows no `btrfs_release_path(path)`, `btrfs_free_path(path)`, or equivalent unlock/release on the `out:` path before `iget_failed(inode)`, the function can call inode eviction while still holding the btree path lock, matching the described ABBA deadlock root cause. Therefore the bug is present, and the fix is not present in this commit.
